ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the circuit diagram there is a series-pass transistor regulator; the left input terminal is labeled +10 V / Vin; the transistor is provided a reference by a Zener diode below labeled 6.6 V; the right load resistor is labeled RL = 10 Ω, connected between the output terminal and ground. Reasoning: According to the Zener reference in the diagram, the transistor emitter/output voltage is approximately Vout = 6.6 V - 0.6 V = 6.0 V. The load current IL = Vout / RL = 6.0 / 10 = 0.6 A. The voltage drop borne by the transistor is Vin - Vout = 10 - 6 = 4 V. Therefore the transistor dissipated power P = 4 × 0.6 = 2.4 W.
